documents.title: Potential impact of AI on our academic mission
documents.stance_why: The Provost writes that "instructors may choose whether or not to allow the use of AI tools and to what extent" and that "the University is not prescribing specific AI policies", so the university sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors; it only asks them to be clear and points to the Academic Code for unapproved use.
documents.summary: A 2023 Provost letter that points to resources on usage, integrity, citation, data protection, research use and IP. It leaves the allow-or-not decision to instructors and ends by encouraging experimentation.

units.why: The Provost says instructors "may choose whether or not to allow the use of AI tools", so the decision sits with each instructor; this is P04 (per-instructor rule), not P02, because no default is set.
units.anchor: instructors may choose whether or not to allow the use of AI tools
units.frag_start: There is a diversity of practice

units.why: "the University is not prescribing specific AI policies" states that no university-wide rule is set, which is the delegation itself; coded P04 because the choice is handed to faculty.
units.anchor: While the University is not prescribing specific AI policies
units.policy: The University does not prescribe specific AI policies.

units.why: "faculty should offer clear, unambiguous information about what is, and is not, allowed" directs instructors to state their AI rules to students, which matches P09 (state AI expectations).
units.anchor: faculty should offer clear, unambiguous information about what is, and is not, allowed

units.why: The Sheridan Center "provides sample syllabus language as well as other tips for classroom integration", an advisory resource for instructors; P63 (support faculty) fits better than P09 because it supplies help, not a duty.
units.anchor: provides sample syllabus language as well as other tips for classroom integration
units.policy: The Sheridan Center provides sample syllabus language and tips for classroom integration.

units.why: "Any unapproved use of AI to complete assignments would be covered by" the Academic Code ties unapproved AI use to the integrity code, so P36 (misconduct) is the type.
units.anchor: Any unapproved use of AI to complete assignments would be covered by

units.why: The concern that students do "work that they then present as something they created without AI assistance" defines the misuse in plain terms (passing AI work off as one's own), so P19 with modality informs.
units.anchor: work that they then present as something they created without AI assistance
units.policy: A common concern is students using AI to do work they then present as something they created without AI assistance.

units.why: "you should give special attention to how you acknowledge and cite the output" asks users who choose AI to acknowledge it, which is disclosure (P24); not P25 because no required detail is listed.
units.anchor: you should give special attention to how you acknowledge and cite the output

units.why: The Library "has compiled general guidelines for citing AI-generated content", which points to citation help; P24 (disclose/cite) is the nearest type and the statement is informational.
units.anchor: The Library has compiled general
units.policy: The Library has compiled guidelines for citing AI-generated content, including guidance from the three major style guides.

units.why: "AI tools are often web services that can store, learn from, and possibly re-share the data you share with them" warns about data exposure, which is P50 (protect data).
units.anchor: can store, learn from, and possibly re-share the data you share with them

units.why: OIT "provides guidance on how to make sure you are not exposing important or sensitive data", pointing users to data-protection guidance, so P50.
units.anchor: how to make sure you are not exposing important or sensitive data
units.policy: OIT provides guidance on making sure users do not expose important or sensitive data to AI services.

units.why: "there are also a number of challenges and risks to understand when using these tools in the research domain" speaks to research use, which is P62 (research and scholarship).
units.anchor: challenges and risks to understand when using these tools in the research domain

units.why: Brown investigators "should be cognizant of the various intellectual property issues" of AI in research; the subject is IP, so P52 rather than P62.
units.anchor: should be cognizant of the various intellectual property issues

units.why: "I encourage all of you to experiment with AI to find ways it could be helpful to your academic experience" openly encourages use, so P02 and encourage.
units.anchor: I encourage all of you to experiment with AI

units.why: "we must also ensure these tools are understood and used appropriately and ethically" sets a principle for the university, which is a framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: we must also ensure these tools are understood and used appropriately and ethically

units.why: Defines generative AI as "open-access tools that can generate realistic text, computer code, and other content", setting what the message covers, so P61.
units.anchor: open-access tools that can generate realistic text, computer code, and other content

units.why: "as we monitor the evolution of these tools" signals ongoing review of AI guidance, matching P54 (revisit regularly).
units.anchor: as we monitor the evolution of these tools
units.policy: The Provost's office will monitor the evolution of AI tools.

units.why: "Please feel free to send additional comments, questions, or concerns" invites feedback to the Provost, which is P54 (feedback invited).
units.anchor: Please feel free to send additional comments, questions, or concerns

documents.title: GAITL report and next steps for GenAI
documents.stance_why: The memo only reports committee findings and recommends "university-wide baseline policies" while "preserving departmental and faculty autonomy"; it states no rule on AI use itself, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: A July 2026 Provost memo summarizing the GAITL report: survey and syllabus findings, six recommendations in three phases, and next steps of drafting syllabus templates. It is a plan, not a rule set.

units.why: The memo says "Brown should establish university-wide baseline policies for GenAI use", a plan for an institution-wide framework (P56) with no rule yet in force.
units.anchor: Brown should establish university-wide baseline policies for GenAI use

units.why: "preserving departmental and faculty autonomy to set localized standards for their specific courses" leaves the rule to departments and faculty, which is P04.
units.anchor: preserving departmental and faculty autonomy to set localized standards for their specific courses

units.why: "expanding secure, enterprise-level AI tools through the Office of Information Technology" is about university-provided AI tools; I chose P17 (sanctioned tool) rather than P51 although "equitable access" is also named, because the action is providing tools.
units.anchor: expanding secure, enterprise-level AI tools through the Office of Information Technology

units.why: "formally update the College and Graduate School academic codes to explicitly address boundaries of AI assistance" would put AI boundaries into the integrity codes; closest is P36 (AI misuse handled under the code).
units.anchor: update the College and Graduate School academic codes to explicitly address boundaries of AI assistance

units.why: "develop and administer additional specialized training to support faculty and staff AI literacy" is faculty support, matching P63.
units.anchor: develop and administer additional specialized training to support faculty and staff AI literacy

units.why: A reconstituted committee will "propose and draft potential syllabi templates" that faculty can choose from, which leaves choice to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: propose and draft potential syllabi templates

units.why: "more than half did not state a policy around GenAI use in teaching and learning" reports evidence from the syllabus audit, so P55 (evidence).
units.anchor: more than half did not state a policy around GenAI use in teaching and learning

units.why: Students "did not indicate a desire for an unregulated digital environment" and asked for structure and training; this is feedback evidence (P55).
units.anchor: did not indicate a desire for an unregulated digital environment

units.why: Both groups worry that "over-reliance on AI may reduce long-term critical thinking", giving a learning rationale for limits (P41).
units.anchor: over-reliance on AI may reduce long-term critical thinking

units.why: "exploring a coalition of peer higher education institutions to help set national standards" is an institution-level framework item, P56.
units.anchor: exploring a coalition of peer higher education institutions to help set national standards

units.why: "investigating a formal AI Literacy undergraduate course designation" is about teaching AI literacy in the curriculum; no type covers curriculum for AI literacy, so UNCOVERED (P44 is about employer-expected AI skill).
units.anchor: investigating a formal "AI Literacy" undergraduate course designation
units.policy: Brown will investigate a formal AI Literacy undergraduate course designation.
units.uncovered_note: Curricular AI-literacy designation or course; not a rule about student AI use.

units.why: "any plan must be viewed as a living document that we will continually refine" says the plan will change, P54.
units.anchor: any plan must be viewed as a living document that we will continually refine

documents.unit: Generative AI in Teaching and Learning Committee
documents.title: GAITL Committee Final Report
documents.stance_why: The report recommends baseline rules but states that "This professional judgment of instructors should supersede University baseline rules" and leaves departments and instructors to decide; no binding stance on student AI use is set, so delegates.

units.policy: Brown-licensed Google Gemini accounts were used to protect data privacy and intellectual property rights.

documents.title: Teaching with AI in Mind (communicating your AI policy)
documents.stance_why: The page offers five sample syllabus statements ("No AI", "Allowed as an Aid to Learning", "Documented Uses Allowed", "Varies by Assignment", "Varies by Student Goals") and a drafting tool for instructors to choose from, so it sets no stance of its own.
tiers: Allowed as an Aid to Learning
documents.summary: Sheridan Center page from the GAITL Phase 2 Committee with sample syllabus statements, an AI Policy Explorer tool, and tips for communicating the policy. The sample statements come from individual courses and carry the policies coded here.

units.why: The page says it is "critical for student learning and ensuring academic integrity that instructors communicate clearly what uses of GenAI are allowed", an expectation that instructors state their rules (P09).
units.anchor: communicate clearly what uses of GenAI are allowed in their course and which are not

units.why: "the same instructor might hold different positions depending on the course they are teaching, or the assignments they have set" says the stance varies by course and assignment (P04).
units.anchor: the same instructor might hold different positions depending on the course they are teaching

units.why: The "No AI" sample says "Students are expected not to use GenAI tools for any work in this course", a ban on all work, so P01 and prohibit.
units.anchor: Students are expected not to use GenAI tools for any work in this course

units.why: The exception "so embedded in the applications or systems they use (such as spellcheck or google search) that they cannot be avoided" addresses AI built into everyday tools, so P07; it permits what cannot be avoided.
units.anchor: so embedded in the applications or systems they use (such as spellcheck or google search)

units.why: "Optional embedded AI Assistants should not be used for core learning activities and assignments" restricts built-in assistants, so P07.
units.anchor: Optional embedded AI Assistants should not be used for core learning activities and assignments
units.frag_end: summarizing readings or conducting literature searches).

units.why: The CSCI 2200 sample "permits (but does not require) the use of these tools as an aid to the learning process", a default of permitted use (P02).
units.anchor: This course permits (but does not require) the use of these tools as an aid

units.why: "If you choose to use generative AI tools, you must disclose such use" is a disclosure duty with each use, P24.
units.anchor: If you choose to use generative AI tools, you must disclose such use

units.why: Use is allowed "only to supplement—never to replace—your own intellectual work", which keeps the student as the main thinker (P32).
units.anchor: only to supplement—never to replace—your own intellectual work
units.policy: AI use may only supplement, never replace, the student's own intellectual work.

units.why: "your work must be consistent with Brown's academic code" ties AI use to the code, which sets the integrity process (P36).
units.anchor: your work must be consistent with Brown's academic code

units.why: The "fellow student" test, "appropriate to have a fellow student (or non-generative AI technology) perform the same task", treats AI like a human helper under existing norms (P45).
units.anchor: appropriate to have a fellow student (or non-generative AI technology) perform the same task

units.why: "the AI-generated answer should be treated as a finding aid only" tells students not to rely on AI answers, closest to P31 (verify output).
units.anchor: the AI-generated answer should be treated as a finding aid only
units.frag_end: relying on it in an assignment).

units.why: "the original source should always be consulted" requires checking the underlying source rather than trusting the AI, P31.
units.anchor: the original source should always be consulted
units.frag_end: relying on it in an assignment).

units.why: "use generative AI tools to create summaries, look up information" allows AI for summaries and lookup, i.e. study-aid uses (P14).
units.anchor: use generative AI tools to create summaries, look up information

units.why: "or to generate ideas" within the same sentence adds idea generation as an allowed use, P15.
units.anchor: or to generate ideas
units.policy: Students may use generative AI tools to generate ideas.

units.why: "your writing must be your own work, describing your own ideas" bars AI from producing the submitted writing, P19.
units.anchor: your writing must be your own work, describing your own ideas

units.why: "it would be fine to use a generative AI tool to perform these functions" allows AI for spelling, grammar and word choice, a prose rule (P18).
units.anchor: Likewise, it would be fine to use a generative AI tool to perform these functions

units.why: "you may not use an AI tool for such redrafting either" forbids AI redrafting of text, so P19.
units.anchor: you may not use an AI tool for such redrafting either

units.why: "you must document and disclose any use of generative AI tools, even if you think it is clear that your use is permitted" requires disclosure for every use, P24.
units.anchor: you must document and disclose any use of generative AI tools

units.why: "questions about whether a particular use of AI is or isn't allowed, please ask!" tells students to ask first, P10.
units.anchor: questions about whether a particular use of AI is or isn't allowed, please ask!

units.why: ENGN 1860 says "Using AI is not discouraged, but should be used with caution", a permissive default with caution (P02, not P03).
units.anchor: Using AI is not discouraged, but should be used with caution

units.why: "AI gets it wrong, so make sure that you check the AI for accuracy" requires checking AI output (P31).
units.anchor: AI gets it wrong, so make sure that you check the AI for accuracy

units.why: "Using AI as an additional source to help you understand the material" allows AI as a tutor for concepts, P12.
units.anchor: Using AI as an additional source to help you understand the material

units.why: "or to help you prepare for an exam is great" allows AI for exam preparation, a study aid (P14).
units.anchor: or to help you prepare for an exam is great

units.why: "Using AI to proof-read or to format a document is fine" allows proofreading and formatting, a prose and formatting rule (P18).
units.anchor: Using AI to proof-read or to format a document is fine

units.why: "using AI to generate content for an assignment is terrible for your learning, and is strictly prohibited" bans AI-produced submitted content, P19.
units.anchor: generate content for an assignment is terrible for your learning, and is strictly prohibited

units.why: "you must include either a specific citation (as you would cite a paper or textbook)" requires citing AI use, P24.
units.anchor: you must include either a specific citation (as you would cite a paper or textbook)

units.why: "document your usage (prompt history etc) with a footnote or appendix for more extensive uses" asks for prompt histories, P26.
units.anchor: document your usage (prompt history etc) with a footnote or appendix for more extensive uses

units.why: "Make sure you maintain the human-in-the-loop" keeps the student as primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: Make sure you maintain the "human-in-the-loop"

units.anchor: you must be able to defend and explain your work in a verbal face-to-face conversation

units.why: "called on in class or in private to present and/or explain their submissions" is a check of understanding by spoken explanation, P34.
units.anchor: called on in class or in private to present and/or explain their submissions

units.why: LANG 2900 states "permitted GenAI use will vary by assignment", so the rule is set per assignment (P04).
units.anchor: permitted GenAI use will vary by assignment

units.why: Assignment guidelines may be "developed in dialogue with students, who may also propose appropriate uses of GenAI", which makes the rule per assignment and negotiated (P04).
units.anchor: developed in dialogue with students, who may also propose appropriate uses of GenAI

units.why: "its use should always support, not replace, your own intellectual work" keeps the student the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: its use should always support, not replace, your own intellectual work

units.why: "inappropriate use of GenAI can undermine the learning process and limit opportunities for meaningful feedback and assessment" gives the learning rationale, P41.
units.anchor: inappropriate use of GenAI can undermine the learning process and limit opportunities

units.anchor: If you are unsure whether a particular use of GenAI is permitted

units.why: "All AI usage in this course must align with the policies defined in the academic code and the student code" ties AI use to the codes, P36.
units.anchor: All AI usage in this course must align with the policies defined in

units.policy: Course staff will not debug LLM code and cannot assist students who cannot explain their code.

units.why: "you may choose to use the assistance of LLMs or not" leaves the choice to the student, a permissive choice (P02).
units.anchor: you may choose to use the assistance of LLMs or not

units.why: "you must attribute the authorship of the work to the AI tool if you choose to use it" requires attribution, P24.
